skills.name: Use the remainder theorem and the factor theorem

note.text:
Remainder theorem: when f(x) is divided by (x − k), the remainder is f(k).
Dividing by (x + k) means x − (−k), so the remainder is f(−k).
Factor theorem: (x − k) is a factor of f(x) exactly when f(k) = 0.
Example: f(x) = x³ − 7x + 6. f(1) = 1 − 7 + 6 = 0, so (x − 1) is a factor. f(3) = 27 − 21 + 6 = 12, so dividing by (x − 3) leaves 12.
Unknown coefficients: if (x − 2) is a factor, put f(2) = 0 and solve for the unknown.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to find a remainder without dividing, decide whether (x − k) is a factor, and find an unknown coefficient.
Builds on: Lesson {12} (dividing a polynomial by x − k).
Leads to: Lesson {14} (factorising cubics) and Lesson {15} (solving cubic equations).

sections.heading: Why the remainder is f(k)
sections.text:
Long division gives f(x) = (x − k) × quotient + remainder.
Put x = k: the bracket (x − k) becomes {0}, so f(k) = {0} × quotient + remainder = remainder.
So to find the remainder when f(x) = {cubic(1, 0, -7, 6)} is divided by x − {3}, just work out f({3}) = {27} − {21} + {6} = {12}.
For a divisor x + {2}, think of it as x − ({-2}): the remainder is f({-2}).

sections.heading: The factor theorem
sections.text:
If the remainder is {0}, the divisor goes exactly: it is a factor.
• f(x) = {cubic(1, 0, -7, 6)}: f({1}) = {1} − {7} + {6} = {0}, so x − {1} is a factor.
• f({2}) = {8} − {14} + {6} = {0}, so x − {2} is a factor too.
Finding an unknown: if x − {2} is a factor of x³ + ax − {6}, then f({2}) = {8} + {2}a − {6} = {0}, so a = {-1}.

The factor theorem tells you at once: work out f({k}) and see whether it is {0}.

solution: Factor theorem: (x − {k}) is a factor exactly when f({k}) = {0}.

misconceptions.explain: Divide by {k * k}, the coefficient of a.

solution: {mono(k * k, 'a')} = {-(k ^ 3) - (q - p * k) * k + q * k}, so a = {answer}.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x³ + ax + b. (x + {2}) is a factor of f(x), and the remainder on dividing f(x) by (x − {1}) is {9 + 3 * a}. Find a.

misconceptions.explain: {8 + 2 * a} is b. The question asks for a.

solution: Substitute b: {1} + a + {8} + {2}a = {9 + 3 * a}, so {3}a = {3 * a} and a = {answer}.
